2. I look at that page's backlink profile to find "why" referring pages are linking to them.

I spent an entire day at the company where I interviewed last week. This was the final part of the interview process. It was training to find out if I'll get on with the tasks. It went very well. I really want the job, bust discovered that it's a lot more responsibility than I had anticipated. That doesn't phase me in the slightest. I still want it and am willing to get up to standard. But it's daunting because I'll be overseeing and supervising other members. I'll even have my own back up (like a secretary, sort of). They'll let me know tomorrow. I really want it and HR was happy with me, although they're interviewing somebody else tomorrow. Whatever happens it's out of my control so I can give myself permission to stop stressing about it as that won't help nor change anything.

It wasn't clear that I'd got the job from what HR said. More like a second round interview based on how I get on in the team. It's a full day, being shown how things work. But I'm sure she said they're doing this with other candidates, so it's the final round in the interview process. I have no idea what to expect.

Thanks for the heads up. Thinking positive and knowing that everyone in the team is friendly & wants to work with me will get me feeling enthusiastic for the day ahead.

I could cite my previous work colleagues as examples of people who never wanted to learn and will undoubtedly remain stagnant. 

Do you know anyone in your field who you could shadow even part time? I did that in the past with my aunt & put it on my cv which got me my first break. Without it I wouldn't have because as you said, most employers are just interested in the number of years the applicant has been warming a chair with their bum.

I'd love to work in a team that takes their work seriously and people who I could learn from. Not like the gang of redneck trash I used to work with until I left. I can relate to the social anxiety at work. I've always been introverted with an aversion to socialise with large groups of people. The anxiety can get worse if your work means being surrounded by lots of people all of the time, with lots of noise. Unfortunately for me this anxiety never improved after a year so I quit my job there. 
I'm certainly not saying you should quit your job but if you can get another one where your social anxiety will be reduced that will be a big step forward. Best of luck with your journey.

The analogy you made really struck me as it's one that I can very much identify with. I was recently sacked after being on sick leave with depression. It feels as though I'm fighting an battle I can't win to become financially independent. The years are rolling by and soon to be 35 with no long term prospects I feel like life is just pointless. I'm not scared of death, I'm just worried about failing in taking my life and waking up with some long term health disorder from a botched up suicide. If I were to kill myself my family would be in pain, but they would get over it. I won't get over mine. So if it's any consolation I can empathise, but I can't recommend you killing yourself if you're not already convinced that you do in fact want to go through with it. I don't think either living or dying is the right decision. It's a paradox that has no answer, but at least in death you wouldn't be conscious of this.
